correctness.rationale: The sixteen independent signed-Bernoulli matrices were classified by occupied-entry count. This gives exactly four possible squared least singular values and yields the stated expectation and determinant-zero probability algebraically. A completed-square inequality proves the sharp relative floor uniquely at (a,b)=(1/2,1/2). On fixed norm s<=1, the derivative of the loss is controlled by h(u)=(3u^2-1)/(4u(u^2-1)), strictly decreasing to 5/(4 sqrt(2)), proving exactly the symmetric-to-asymmetric optimizer transition. Symbolic full enumeration, 121 exact rational tests, 1000 direct-SVD comparisons and six orientation checks were actually rerun from the embedded verification script. Infinite/general claims rest on the analytic proof, not simulations.

value.rationale: Recent numerical-analysis work treats stochastic rounding as a possible tail-spectrum regularizer. The complete minimum-dimensional, perfectly conditioned, independent-rounded rotation exposes why such a claim cannot be unconditional: the smallest squared singular value loses up to (sqrt(5)-1)/4 of its expectation, even as total squared energy increases; the rounded system is singular with probability 9/16 at the unique worst relative input. The additional exact orientation bifurcation gives a concrete coordinate-system sensitivity criterion. This is a structural boundary and sharp design law for a natural model, not a textbook deduction or an arbitrary small parameter instance. Claims are limited to this model and do not imply real-hardware instability.
